content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text discusses whether the loins/seed row was answered and whether [DR3] pressed it, but it does not count any cited-in verse as an unanswered witness or toward a broken link.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.", "room": "'unanswered witness': either the rule governs only an express count of a cited-in verse as unanswered or broken, or it governs any discussion of answered/pressed verses; the text makes no such count.", "why": "The judge says the row was answered and does not count Acts 2:30 or any pressed verse as an unanswered witness or broken link, so not counting it is permitted."}
